output.title: Late payment terms are a workflow problem, not just finance
output.body:
Late payment terms often show up first as a workflow problem, not a finance problem. For an owner of a small business, the useful question is not “are the terms bad?” but “which repeated task is creating the drag: invoice tracking, payment-chasing emails, or an aging report in a spreadsheet?” That is the bounded decision worth looking at first.

If the task is repeatable, measurable, and mostly the same each time, it may be a candidate for AI or workflow automation. If it changes a lot from case to case, or if the step touches money movement, keep human approval in place and leave that part manual. That is not a failure; it is basic control.

Bareni’s normal sequence is a free diagnostic, then a one-page pilot proposal, then a working MVP if the workflow fits. Those timings are intended scopes, not guarantees, and the diagnostic can also conclude that AI is not the right tool.

A practical next step: write down the last five overdue-payment cases and ask one question about each one — was the follow-up the same every time? If yes, you have a workflow to examine. If no, you have a judgment call that probably stays human. Dry, but useful.
